title: Topic vocabulary: cities and urban life

guide.p: City life is a favourite topic in Task 2 and Part 3: traffic, housing costs, green spaces, moving from the countryside, and how to plan better cities. These words help you describe problems and propose solutions.

bullets: Learn words in phrases, not alone: notice which verbs, adjectives and prepositions go with them.
Practise each word in a sentence about your own life or country — it will be easier to use in Speaking.
In Writing, choose the precise word over the impressive-sounding one. Accuracy beats complexity.

guide.tip: 'Urban' means of a city; 'rural' means of the countryside. 'Suburban' areas are at the edge of a city.

vocab.meaning: the movement of people from the countryside to cities
vocab.example: Rapid urbanisation has put pressure on housing.

vocab.meaning: basic systems such as roads, water and power
vocab.example: The city needs to invest in its infrastructure.

vocab.meaning: too much traffic, causing slow movement
vocab.example: Congestion charges have reduced traffic in the centre.

vocab.meaning: the busiest times for travel to and from work
vocab.example: The trains are packed during rush hour.

vocab.meaning: a person who travels regularly to work
vocab.example: Thousands of commuters arrive by train each morning.

vocab.meaning: buses, trains and trams available to everyone
vocab.example: Good public transport reduces car use.

vocab.meaning: a person walking; for people walking (adjective)
vocab.example: The main street is now a pedestrian zone.

vocab.meaning: part of a road reserved for bicycles
vocab.example: New cycle lanes have made cycling safer.

vocab.meaning: a residential area on the edge of a city
vocab.example: Many families move to the suburbs for more space.

vocab.meaning: the uncontrolled spread of a city into the countryside
vocab.example: Urban sprawl increases dependence on cars.

vocab.meaning: a very tall building with many floors
vocab.example: High-rise flats house thousands of people on a small site.

vocab.meaning: homes that people on average incomes can afford
vocab.example: There is a serious shortage of affordable housing.

vocab.meaning: the money needed for basic expenses
vocab.example: The cost of living in the capital is very high.

vocab.meaning: having too many people in a space
vocab.example: Overcrowding in flats can affect children's health.

vocab.meaning: the state of having no home
vocab.example: Homelessness has risen as rents increased.

vocab.meaning: useful facilities such as shops, parks and libraries
vocab.example: The new estate lacks basic amenities.

vocab.meaning: an area of grass and trees in a town
vocab.example: Green spaces help to cool the city in summer.

vocab.meaning: an area mainly of homes
vocab.example: Lorries are banned from residential areas at night.

vocab.meaning: harmful or annoying levels of noise
vocab.example: Noise pollution from the airport disturbs residents.

vocab.meaning: improving a run-down area
vocab.example: The regeneration of the docks created thousands of jobs.

vocab.meaning: change in a poor area as wealthier people move in, often raising prices
vocab.example: Gentrification has pushed long-term residents out.

vocab.meaning: the central, often older and poorer, part of a city
vocab.example: Inner-city schools face particular challenges.

vocab.meaning: of the countryside
vocab.example: Rural areas often have fewer bus services.

vocab.meaning: the organisation that governs a town or area
vocab.example: The local authority is responsible for rubbish collection.
